doc.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-04-02

title: First jobs with Arnold DePass fraternity dance bands
summary: De De's first jobs were with drummer Arnold DePass playing fraternity dances on St. Charles Avenue; he names sidemen Bill Phillips, George Stewart, Johnny Dave and Reese Cobet.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Do you remember your very first job that you played on the trumpet?
Playing with Arnold DePass, he's not deceased. He was an old time drummer too, an old drummer.

He used to play those fraternity dances at any time all along St. Charles Avenue. You know, and you get all those fraternities, different organizations. And that's how I began to play out, like one job to another.
Do you remember who else was in those bands? No. That early band, Arnold DePox?

There's a, let me see, a guy which is called Bill Phillips, drummer. I don't know if he's working anymore, if he's still living. You see that drummer. I heard the door. I don't know if he's in sax. Oh, oh, oh, oh, oh, oh. Don't you remember when you work with Billy? The old man, he smoked him in cigarettes.
Oh, oh, oh, oh. George Stewart. Huh?
George Stewart. What did he play?

Clarinet? Sax. Sax. Most of the clarinet in that time, but he played a little sax too also. That George Stewart. I don't know if he's still living yet. I don't know. And one of the Dave, like Johnny Dave, banjo. Oh, yeah.
There was a Cobet tour, a Reese Cobet. I don't know if he's in this city, he left four years ago too. Fat fella, saxophone player too. Cobet.
